extracted.intended_audience: comedy industry professionals, performers (stand-ups, character acts, digital creators, writers), and comedy fans following festival lineups
extracted.subtask_description: A news summary of Just For Laughs' New Faces of Comedy Showcase selections for 2025, describing the categories, selection focus, and how selected participants will be presented at the festival. Useful for performers, agents, and industry professionals tracking emerging comedic talent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and promise
rubrics_metrics.description: "Each year, we sift through thousands of names from across the world to find the most original and promising comedic voices," said Nick Brazao, Head of Programming & Talent, Just For Laughs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection emphasizes originality and promise as primary qualities; the program looks globally and considers a large applicant/pool size. (Verbatim quote indicates evaluative lens used by programming.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Breakout / career potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Since its inception in 1994, New Faces has been regarded as a premier launchpad, helping to propel the careers of dozens of comedy’s biggest stars — among them, Kevin Hart, Amy Schumer, Ali Wong, Jo Koy, and Kumail Nanjiani.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates are implicitly evaluated for their potential to break out commercially/industry-wise; historical alumni are cited to show the program seeks acts likely to advance to larger careers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category — Stand Ups (rising stand-up comics)
rubrics_metrics.description: This year’s program will continue to spotlight rising stand-up comics ... (lists the selected stand-ups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stand-up selections focus on rising performers; examples and cross-references (e.g., inclusion of comics previously listed as 'Comedians Ready To Break Out In 2025') indicate editors/programming look for momentum and prior recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category — Characters (character performers)
rubrics_metrics.description: New Faces: Characters — selection of character performers (lists selected names).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programming separately recognizes character-based performers distinct from straight stand-ups, implying evaluation of character work, sketch/performative ability, and persona-driven comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category — Creators (emerging digital and social media comedy voices)
rubrics_metrics.description: New Faces: Creators highlights emerging digital and social media comedy voices, character performers, and original-format innovators who are redefining how comedy is made and shared. (Presented in partnership with SMOSH.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection for this category values digital-native formats, social-media reach/innovation, and original-format creativity; partnerships (SMOSH) suggest industry-aligned curation and consideration of platform-native metrics or format innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category — Writers (rising scripted comedy talent)
rubrics_metrics.description: New Faces: Writers, spotlighting rising talent in scripted comedy. Selected writers will bring their original half-hour scripts to life in live table reads featuring fellow New Faces performers. (In partnership with More Better.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation centers on scripted-writing ability and originality of half-hour scripts; expectation that writers submit original half-hour material suitable for table reads and live performance, with industry partnership indicating development/production interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection scope and presentation context
rubrics_metrics.description: The New Faces showcases will take place as part of JFL’s ComedyPRO industry programming between July 23 and July 26, with the festival running through the 27th. The program sifts through thousands of names from across the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is global and competitive; chosen acts are presented within industry-facing programming (ComedyPRO), implying criteria include suitability for industry showcases, live-read/readiness, and timing within festival scheduling.
